algorithm.failure: a nonzero payload status is returned verbatim and the closing brace is not appended; the buffer keeps {"Ip": plus whatever partial payload the writer appended
algorithm.framing: in order: '{', '"', the two key bytes, '"', ':', the payload appended by the payload writer, then '}' — the exact success byte sequence is {"Ip":<payload>}
algorithm.growth_gate: before each of the five inline single-byte appends ('{', both quotes, ':', '}') the routine compares the buffer length with its capacity and, only on equality, calls the grow helper 0x5963a10 with (rdi = buffer, edx = 1, ecx = 1, r8d = 1), reloads the length, and appends without re-testing capacity
algorithm.key_append: the key is the only part not appended inline: append-bytes helper 0x50a3510(buffer, 0x93a200, 2); the length is reloaded from the buffer after the call
algorithm.payload: payload writer 0x50a2ad0(rdi = the routine's rdi, rsi = the routine's rsi) appends the payload into the same buffer; the routine reloads the buffer length before the closing brace
algorithm.success_status: on the success path the returned value is the payload writer's 0, saved in r14 at 0x5a30099 and restored at 0x5a300a1 across the closing-brace grow call

consumers.inspected_setup: at 3 of the 6 sites the caller appends JSON punctuation to the same buffer immediately before the transfer ('[' written inline at 0x5045987 and 0x5045aa1, ':' at 0x5072eeb), so the routine writes one member/element inside larger serializers; at 0x5072f04 the payload pointer rdi is the caller's rbx advanced by one when the byte at [rbx] is nonzero (a leading tag byte is skipped)
consumers.sites: 5 direct calls and 1 tail jump in 5 caller FDEs (callers.tsv); the tail jump at 0x5080e6a makes the caller's return value this routine's return value

object_layout.context: rsi points at a context whose +0x00 word is the output buffer pointer; the same context pointer is forwarded to the payload writer; this routine reads no other context field
object_layout.output_buffer: +0x00 capacity in bytes, +0x08 data pointer, +0x10 length in bytes; the routine reads all three and stores the length back after every append it performs itself

routines.inputs: rdi = opaque payload source (forwarded untouched to the payload writer, never dereferenced here), rsi = context pointer whose first word is the output buffer
routines.name: JSON writer for the Ip variant
routines.outputs: rax = the payload writer's status verbatim; on the success path 0, returned after the closing brace is appended

strings.key: 0x93a200: the two bytes 'Ip', a pointer+length constant in the packed .rodata string table (not NUL-terminated; the next packed string begins at 0x93a202)

unknowns: The payload bytes and whether they are quoted: the payload writer's body is not pinned. Its head reads four bytes from rdi and formats decimal digits around '.' separators on its stack, consistent with a dotted-decimal IPv4 rendering, but this packet claims only the forwarding and status contract.
The grow helper's capacity policy: only the call contract (invoked on length == capacity with arguments 1, 1, 1; the append then proceeds without a re-check) is pinned.
The append-bytes helper's internal growth and failure behavior; the routine relies on it for the key and reloads the length afterwards.
Whether the buffer length can ever exceed its capacity: the routine tests equality only, so the length <= capacity invariant is assumed, not enforced, in the observed code.
The caller bodies beyond the three inspected argument setups, and the meaning of the tag byte skipped at the 0x5072f04 site.
What the payload writer reads from the context beyond the buffer word at +0x00.
